summary: Nubes (Latin for "cloud") is the cloud-mate Hyginus names with Ixion as parent of wild centaurs such as Nessus and Eurytion. She corresponds to the unnamed cloud Zeus shaped in Hera's likeness in Apollodorus — the mother of Centaurus — and must be distinguished from Nephele, the cloud-wife of Athamas who bore Phrixus and Helle.
etymology: Latin nubes, "cloud"; Greek counterpart νεφέλη (nephélē), "cloud." The atlas id nubes-ixion marks the Ixion genealogy against the Athamantid Nephele.

sections.heading: Ixion and the false Hera
paragraphs: When Ixion lusts after Hera, Zeus forms a cloud in the goddess's image. Ixion couples with the cloud; punishment (binding to a fiery wheel) follows the outrage against hospitality and the queen of heaven.
Apollodorus says the cloud bears Centaurus, who then fathers the horse-men on Magnesian mares. The cloud herself is usually left unnamed in that account.

sections.heading: Hyginus' Nubes
paragraphs: Hyginus Fabulae names Nubes explicitly as mother, with Ixion, of centaurs including Nessus and others of the wild brood. In that Latin handbook the cloud is a genealogical parent rather than a silent prop.
The atlas keeps this Hyginus naming under nubes-ixion so that centaur parent edges can point at a stable node without collapsing her into the Boeotian Nephele.

sections.heading: Homonym: Nephele of Athamas
paragraphs: Nephele, first wife of Athamas and mother of Phrixus and Helle, is a different cloud-nymph with a separate myth (the golden ram, the Hellespont). Sharing the language of clouds does not make the two figures one person; sources and children diverge cleanly.
Reception sometimes speaks loosely of "Nephele" for Ixion's cloud; in this dataset the Athamantid remains nephele and the Ixion mate remains nubes-ixion.
